note: Window agent p1800-p1809, 2 Nov 2026. Most entries repair one dossier defect: a keyframe whose text says 'for 1800 only' (or 'for 1802 only') but which keeps Cliopatria's longer span, so that the compiler's union of the keyframes alive in a year keeps the old shape (Piedmont as Sardinian 1802-1809, Egypt as French in 1802); the others fill land that two keyframes or events left without an owner (the Misiones Orientales 1800-1809, Santo Domingo 1802-1808, Piedmont at the end of 1802, the Tarnopol Kreis 1809) or settle a conflict the colony rule decided wrongly (the Hejaz 1803-1810, the Croatian Military Frontier 1809).

region.text: the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay river

events.note: 1801: the Misiones Orientales pass from the Portuguese crown's own hands to Brazil. spanish-empire/ledger/71 hands the missions to the portuguese-empire dossier in 1801, and the Brazilian keyframe cannot take cells that an event of the same year moved; from 1803 the portuguese-empire keyframes then release them as ownerless. The page: Portugal accepted the Treaty of Badajoz on 6 June 1801 and the Treaty of Madrid on 29 September 1801, and 'neither Spain nor Portugal gave back the territories acquired both in America (Eastern Missions) and the Peninsula'.

correction.text: for 1800-1801 only: Piedmont and Aosta under French occupation (hatched) with the island; from 1802 the mainland is French and Italian-Republic land, see kingdom-of-sardinia_1802

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own text limits this keyframe to 1800-1801, but with no 'to' it inherits Cliopatria's span 1800-1813 and overlaps the island-only keyframe kingdom-of-sardinia_1802; the compiler unions the keyframes alive in a year, so from 1802 the Sardinian crown is snapped onto all of Piedmont and Aosta and keeps them to 1813. The page: the Subalpine Republic 'ceased to exist on 11 September 1802, when it was divided between the French Republic and the Italian Republic' ('The French Republic annexed the departements of Doire, Marengo, Po, Sesia, Stura, and Tanaro'; the Italian Republic annexed Novara); Charles Emmanuel IV abdicated on 4 June 1802 in favour of Victor Emmanuel I, who was in Cagliari. The keyframe now ends in 1801.

union.text: the former Prince-Bishopric of Basel, French since before 1798: the Helvetic Republic page says the treaty of 19 August 1798 'reaffirmed the French annexation of the Prince-Bishopric of Basel'

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1800 shape plus the Jura (the former Prince-Bishopric of Basel)

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1800 shape (Egypt included) spans 1800-1802 and overlaps the dossier's own 1802 keyframe 'without Egypt'; the union draws Egypt (168 cells) as French again in 1802 after the evacuation. The page: 'Menou capitulated on 2 September' 1801 (Cairo: '27 June ... General Belliard surrenders in Cairo'); the capitulation 'allowed the Army of the Orient to be repatriated to Europe in British ships'. The keyframe now ends in 1801.

union.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1805 inside Brazil
the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay river

correction.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1805 inside Brazil, plus the Misiones Orientales that Portugal conquered in 1801 and kept

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's ledger/21 gives Portugal the Misiones Orientales in 1801 and spanish-empire/ledger/71 takes them from Spain, but this keyframe (Cliopatria's 1805 Portuguese shape inside Brazil) leaves the 226 cells out, so the missions are ownerless from 1800 to the end of the window. The page lists 'Portuguese invasion of Misiones Orientales' among the results of the War of the Oranges (Portugal accepted the Treaty of Badajoz on 6 June 1801 and the Treaty of Madrid on 29 September 1801) and says that 'neither Spain nor Portugal gave back the territories acquired both in America (Eastern Missions) and the Peninsula'.

union.text: the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay river
the former Spanish colony of Santo Domingo, the east of Hispaniola

correction.text: for 1800 only: the Misiones Orientales and Santo Domingo, still Spanish until 1801

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe for 1800 only, unioned with the alive Spanish keyframes. The keyframe spanish-empire_1800 says the Dominican Republic and the Misiones Orientales are 'removed from 1801', but it starts in 1800 and strips both at the end of that year, a year too early. Santo Domingo: 'In January 1801, Louverture and his nephew, General Hyacinthe Moise invaded the Spanish territory, taking possession of it from the governor' (spanish-empire/ledger/72 hands it over in 1801). Misiones: the page War of the Oranges lists the 'Portuguese invasion of Misiones Orientales' among the results of the war of May-June 1801 (spanish-empire/ledger/71).

union.text: the former Spanish colony of Santo Domingo, the east of Hispaniola
Piedmont and the Aosta valley without Novara: the departements of Doire, Marengo, Po, Sesia, Stura and Tanaro

correction.text: Santo Domingo, the east of Hispaniola, and the departements annexed from the Subalpine Republic (Piedmont and Aosta without Novara)

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe, unioned with the alive French keyframes. (1) The page: 'Landing at Santo Domingo with 2,000 men, General Kerverseau took possession of a large part of the Spanish area' (the February 1802 landings); the Santo Domingo page: ceded to France by the Treaty of Basel (22 July 1795), the 'Era de Francia' lasted until 1809. The French keyframes (Cliopatria's overseas-free shapes) leave the east of Hispaniola out, so the keyframe snap of 1802 strips the cells that haiti/ledger/10 gives France and the east stays ownerless from 1802 to 1808. (2) Subalpine Republic page: on 11 September 1802 France annexed the departements Doire, Marengo, Po, Sesia, Stura and Tanaro; the 1802 keyframe omits them, so the 84 Piedmont cells that subalpine-republic/ledger/3 gave France in September are released again at the end of 1802.

correction.text: the former Spanish colony of Santo Domingo, the east of Hispaniola

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe, unioned with the alive empire keyframes, which are drawn 'without overseas cells'. The page: Santo Domingo 'was to be ceded to France' (Treaty of Basel, 22 July 1795; infobox 'annexed to France'); 'This period called the Era de Francia, lasted until 1809 until being recaptured by the Dominican general Juan Sanchez Ramirez' (infobox: 'returned to Spain: 9 July 1809'). Keeps the east French through 1808; spanish-empire/ledger/74-76 contest it from November 1808 and return it in July 1809.

union.text: Chukotka, Russian since the 1778 gain (russian-empire ledger); the override replaced the dossier keyframe that carries it (orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026, fx-43 R126 handoff)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1809-1810 Russian shape plus the whole Tarnopol district that Austria ceded in October 1809; plus Chukotka

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note says 'Tarnopol (TE 1809) [is a] small addition here', and the shape holds only 15 of the 47 cells of the Tarnopoler Kreis (a 60 km circle about Ternopil). The ledger gives Russia the whole district (russian-empire/ledger/51, kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria/ledger/4), but at the end of 1809 the keyframe releases the 32 cells outside the shape and they stay ownerless. The page: Austria ceded 'Tarnopol district to the Russian Empire' by the Treaty of Schoenbrunn (14 October 1809); the shape's span is 1809-1810.

rulings.why: The page: 'Wahhabi forces led by Abdulaziz bin Muhammad Al Saud entered Mecca in 1803 after defeating Ghalib and forcing his surrender' and 'the Wahhabis gained control of Mecca and Medina by 1805'; the Ottoman landing at Yanbu in 1811 is the first Ottoman gain. Habesh Eyalet's keyframe draws the coastal Hejaz as Ottoman for 1557-1864, so R1 (colony wins) gives the emirate's Hejaz claims of 1803 and 1805 to the Ottoman vassal (2,434 cell-years of conflict) and the emirate's own events (Mecca 1803, Medina 1804) find nothing to take. The p1810-p1819 patch (rulings/3) covers 1811-1812 and asks for this ruling for the years before.

region.text: the Croatian lands southwest of the Sava: a polygon whose north-east edge follows the river from the Slovenian border by Zagreb, Sisak and Jasenovac to Stara Gradiska

rulings.why: The page: by the Treaty of Schoenbrunn (14 October 1809) Austria ceded 'the Croatian lands southwest of the river Sava to the French Empire', which became the Illyrian Provinces. The Military Frontier is a colony of Austria and wins the 110 cells by the size rule in 1809 (and 55 in 1810), although the Illyrian keyframe claims them; the provinces run to January 1814 in their dossier. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: region added. Without it the ruling gave all 55 conflict cells to the provinces, 14 of them north-east of the Sava (Koprivnica-Krizevci, Moslavina, Novska), which the treaty did not cede; the ruling now acts on the 41 cells south-west of the river and the rest stay with the Military Frontier.]

region.text: Minnesota north of 47 N (the Red River valley, Red Lake and the Rainy River country) less the Leech Lake pocket inside the Mississippi's upper loop, which lies west of the river

rulings.why: Louisiana, retroceded to France in 1800, ended at the Mississippi: Louisiana Purchase page, 'The eastern boundary of the Louisiana purchase was the Mississippi River, from its source to the 31st parallel', and Minnesota is in the purchase only as 'the portion of Minnesota west of the Mississippi River'; its northern limit was 'Rupert's Land'. Against the current dossiers French Louisiana's found of 1800 (54,069 km2) claims 133 cells of northern Minnesota east of the river that Rupert's Land holds (47.0-49.0 N, 97.1-93.5 W), and the size rule gives them to France for 1800-1803; the United States then inherits them in 1804 and its 1805 shape (which leaves out the Red River valley) releases about 110 of them to nobody for 1805-1809. The Louisiana Purchase page has the United States receive 'parts of the Red River Basin south of 49th parallel' only in the Convention of 1818, so Rupert's Land keeps them (as the p1790-p1799 draft already has them to 1799). This is the same east-bank overshoot of the gazetteer's Louisiana region that p1770-p1779 events/1 and p1780-p1789 rulings/2 repair for Quebec's time.
